fullName: IBPS Customer Service Associate / Clerk Recruitment (CRP CSA)
overview: IBPS Clerk — officially **Customer Service Associate (CSA)** — is the largest recruitment channel for **clerical posts in 11 public sector banks**, run as one Common Recruitment Process every year. Unlike IBPS PO, this is a **state-wise exam**: vacancies are announced state by state, you apply for **one state/UT only**, you must be proficient in that state's local language (checked through a qualifying language test), and the cut-offs are declared **state-wise and category-wise**. There are two online stages — a qualifying Preliminary and a merit-deciding Main — and **no interview**: your final merit is the Main exam score alone. The mains pattern was recently rebuilt around **weighted marks (200 marks, 125 minutes, 160 questions)**, so section value differs per question and the mains, not the prelims, is where selection is actually won. Fixed syllabus, fixed sectional timers, lakhs of applicants per state — this is a speed-and-accuracy game where **shortcuts + sectional drills + state-aware target scores** beat generic study.

If you are appearing, you are in the final-revision window — one timed mock every alternate day, sectional drills on your weak area, and your state's target score pinned above your desk.

statusPhases.status: **Prelims call letters are out on ibps.in (posted 1 October 2026) — download yours and check your city, date and shift.** Exam is reported for 10–11 October 2026. Until your shift: one 60-minute mock every alternate day, a 20-minute sectional drill daily (the 20-minute timers allow no recovery time), formula and rules-revision sheets twice, nothing new in the last 48 hours.

**Prelims done — the result is expected around November 2026.** Do not wait for it to start Mains prep: the mains is a different animal (125 minutes, weighted marks, General/Financial Awareness including current affairs of the last 6–8 months). Begin a daily GA habit and a weekly banking-awareness revision now; the December mains rewards the candidates who used this gap.

**Mains window (call letters expected November 2026, exam December 2026).** Shift fully to mains-weighted practice: Reasoning (60 marks) and Quantitative Aptitude (50 marks) carry the weight, English is 40 marks, General/Financial Awareness 50 marks in just 20 minutes — speed matters most there. Take full 125-minute mocks every 2–3 days with a mistakes notebook.

**Mains done.** Qualifying candidates face the **Local Language Proficiency Test** (qualifying; skipped if you already studied that language in Class 10 or above, with proof) and then **Provisional Allotment, expected around March 2027**. Watch for reserve-list allotments in the following months.

stages.name: Preliminary Examination (Qualifying)
stages.nature: Qualifying — shortlists candidates for the Mains
stages.negative: One-fourth of the marks assigned to the question (−0.25) per wrong answer
stages.notes: Flat **+1 per correct answer**, **−0.25** per wrong answer, with a separate **20-minute timer on each section** — you cannot move between sections or bank time. You must clear the sectional cut-off in each of the three tests **and** land inside the shortlist; IBPS shortlists an adequate number of candidates per category per **state**, depending on that state's vacancies. The prelims score is discarded after shortlisting — only the mains counts in the final merit. Available in English and Hindi plus the regional languages notified for your state.

stages.name: Main Examination (Objective, merit-deciding)
stages.nature: Merit-deciding — mains marks alone form the final merit (no interview)
stages.negative: One-fourth of the marks assigned to the question per wrong answer
stages.notes: This is the **revised mains structure** — 160 questions for 200 marks in 125 minutes, replacing the older 190-question scheme — with **weighted marking**: Reasoning carries 1.5 marks per question, General/Financial Awareness and Quantitative Aptitude 1.25, General English 1.0. Section order is not fixed on screen and each section is separately timed (**20 + 35 + 35 + 35 minutes**). You need a **minimum score in each test and a minimum total**, decided state-wise and category-wise against vacancies, to be considered for provisional allotment. Candidates should expect to be at the venue for about 3 hours including formalities. **Marks obtained in the mains only are considered for the final merit listing.**

stages.name: Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) and Provisional Allotment
stages.nature: Qualifying language test — then merit-based allotment to a bank
stages.mode: Conducted after the mains, by an independent body or the bank
stages.negative: Marks-based but **qualifying only** — failing it removes you from the process
stages.notes: You pick **one** local language at application time from the list for your state/UT. Candidates who have studied that language in **Class 10 or above** (with a mark-sheet/certificate as proof) are exempt from the test. Since there is no interview, the mains merit list flows directly into provisional allotment across the 11 participating banks, honouring state-wise vacancies and reservation norms. Allotment validity runs one year from the date of provisional allotment or until a fresh allotment, whichever is earlier.

selectionProcess: **Prelims (qualifying) → Mains (final merit) → Local Language Proficiency Test (qualifying) → Provisional Allotment.** The prelims filters candidates per state and category through sectional cut-offs plus a shortlist. The mains — 160 questions, 200 marks, 125 minutes — **alone decides the merit**; there is no interview. Mains-qualified candidates then clear the local-language test (unless exempt with Class-10 proof) and IBPS allots them to a participating bank against the vacancies of the applied state/UT. Since marks are normalised across shifts with the equi-percentile method, your state's cut-off — not your raw score — is the number to beat.
normalization: Because the exam runs in many shifts with different papers, IBPS **normalises corrected scores across sessions using the equi-percentile method**, carrying scores to two decimals, before declaring results and cut-offs. Practical reading: (1) never compare raw marks across shifts, years or states; (2) a tough shift is not a penalty — the normalised score is what counts; (3) target scores should come from your **state's** recent cut-offs, which vary enormously (recent prelims cut-offs ranged from the mid-40s to the high-80s out of 100 across states).

faqs.q: Can I apply for more than one state in IBPS Clerk?
faqs.a: No. Recruitment is state/UT-wise and you can apply for vacancies in **only one state or UT**. You must also be proficient in that state's local language — checked through the qualifying LLPT — so pick a state where you have a genuine language and domicile advantage, not just a lower-looking cutoff.

faqs.q: Is there an interview in IBPS Clerk?
faqs.a: No. Selection is **mains-only**: marks obtained in the Main examination alone form the final merit, followed by the qualifying local-language test and provisional allotment. This makes mains accuracy worth more than in PO, where an interview can still rescue a marginal score.

faqs.q: What is the negative marking in IBPS Clerk?
faqs.a: **One-fourth (0.25) of the marks assigned to a question** is deducted for each wrong answer in both stages. Unanswered questions cost nothing. In the mains, where questions are worth up to 1.5 marks, a wrong guess costs proportionally more.

faqs.q: Is there sectional timing and a sectional cut-off?
faqs.a: Yes, in both stages. Prelims: **20 minutes each** for English, Numerical Ability and Reasoning, with a sectional qualifying cut-off in each test plus a state-wise shortlist. Mains: separately-timed sections (20 minutes General/Financial Awareness, then 35 minutes each for English, Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude) with minimum marks per test and a minimum total for the merit consideration.

faqs.q: What is the current mains pattern?
faqs.a: The revised structure is **160 questions / 200 marks / 125 minutes**: General/Financial Awareness 40Q/50M/20 min, General English 40Q/40M/35 min, Reasoning Ability 40Q/60M/35 min, Quantitative Aptitude 40Q/50M/35 min — **weighted marks** (Reasoning 1.5 per question, others 1.25 and 1.0), replacing the older 190-question scheme. Always re-check the current notification; IBPS explicitly reserves the right to change the structure.

faqs.q: What is the Local Language Proficiency Test?
faqs.a: A **qualifying, marks-based test** of your chosen state's local language (reading, writing, speaking, understanding), conducted after the mains and before joining. Candidates who studied that language in **Class 10 or above** and can show the mark-sheet/certificate are exempt. Failing it removes you from the process even with a merit-list rank.

IBPS normalises corrected scores across exam shifts using the **equi-percentile method** (to two decimals), so candidates facing harder papers are not disadvantaged. Published cut-offs are always on normalised scores — comparing raw marks across shifts or years is meaningless.

No. You must already be a graduate **on the day of registration**, with a valid mark-sheet or degree and your exact graduation percentage (to two decimals) filled in the form. Documents are verified later.

faqs.q: Is a computer certificate really required?
faqs.a: Yes — clerical eligibility demands **operating and working knowledge of computers**, evidenced by a certificate/diploma/degree in computer operations or language, **or** Computer/IT as a subject in High School/College/Institute. If your Class 10 or 12 mark-sheet shows Computer/IT as a subject, that itself works as proof.
There is **no attempt limit** — apply every cycle until you cross the age limit (28 for the general category, 31 for OBC, 33 for SC/ST, plus PwBD relaxations).

faqs.q: What salary does an IBPS Clerk get?
faqs.a: Basic pay is **₹24,050** on the clerical scale (₹24,050 – ₹64,480), with dearness allowance, HRA and other allowances as per bank rules. Indicative take-home is around **₹35,000–₹45,000 per month** depending on the bank and city — treat online figures as approximations.

faqs.q: What score should I target in the prelims?
faqs.a: It depends entirely on your state — recent general-category prelims cut-offs have ranged from the **mid-40s** (Gujarat 45.25, Maharashtra 46, Karnataka 46 in 2025) to the **mid-80s** (Chandigarh 86.5, Delhi 84, Uttarakhand 85 in 2025) out of 100. Use your own state's last two years of cut-offs plus a 5–8 mark safety margin, and respect the sectional timers.

faqs.q: How is IBPS Clerk different from IBPS PO?
faqs.a: Clerk is **state-wise** (PO is all-India), has **no interview** (PO: 100-mark interview worth 20%), requires a **local language and computer-literacy proof**, and tests **Numerical Ability** (school-level arithmetic) in the prelims rather than Quantitative Aptitude. Clerk postings stay within your applied state; PO postings can be anywhere in the bank's network.

faqs.q: What documents are needed at joining?
faqs.a: Matriculation certificate (date of birth), graduation mark-sheets and degree, the **computer-literacy proof**, the **local-language Class-10 proof if claiming LLPT exemption**, category certificates in the prescribed format (OBC NCL issued on or after 01.04.2026; EWS income-and-asset certificate for the current year), PwBD/Ex-Servicemen certificates where claimed, and photo ID. Keep the printed prelims and mains call letters too — banks ask for stamped copies at joining.

documents: Across the process, keep ready: **matriculation certificate** (date-of-birth proof), **graduation mark-sheets and degree certificate** with the exact percentage you entered, **computer-literacy certificate** (or mark-sheets showing Computer/IT as a subject), **local-language proof** (Class 10 or above certificate for LLPT exemption), **category certificates** in central-government format — OBC non-creamy-layer issued on or after 01.04.2026, EWS income-and-asset certificate valid for the year, SC/ST/PwBD/Ex-Servicemen certificates as claimed — plus photo ID and printed call letters of both stages. Since allotment is state-wise, your state's language and category documentation must match your application exactly; discrepancies surface at the bank's joining verification.
